title: Agent Primitive Instances inherit a base class of operational logic from the Core Atlas, and upstream edits propagate automatically
content:
Keel's Instance-level Routine Protocols are references, not text. A.6.1.1.3.2.5.1.3.1.2.1 states that the Solana Bridge Instance "inherits the base class of operational logic defined in A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1 - Routine Protocol, subject to the qualifications specified in A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1 - Near-Term Process," and then makes the consequence explicit: "modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to this Instance." The 1inch and Kamino Instances (A.6.1.1.3.2.5.1.3.2.2.1, A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.2.1) use the identical formula against their own base protocols.

The Atlas is borrowing class inheritance from programming, and the borrowed semantics are the point. Sky Core can improve how Distribution Rewards or Integration Boosts operate once, and every Agent Instance that inherits picks up the change without an Artifact Edit Proposal, a Facilitator review, or a tokenholder vote in any Agent.

That is a large amount of unilateral upstream power over an Agent's day-to-day operations, and it is the mirror image of the Artifact Edit Restrictions: Agents cannot edit the Atlas, and the Atlas can edit Agents' operating logic. Consistency across Agents is bought at the price of Agent-level stability.

The clauses also flag the arrangement as provisional — "in future iterations of the Keel Artifact, a version of the full process definition customized to Keel will be included herein." Inlining that text later would trade automatic propagation for local control, which is a real fork in the road, not a formatting cleanup.
description: Each Keel Instance points at Core Atlas protocol logic instead of copying it, so Sky can change how every Agent's incentive programs run without any Agent Artifact being amended.
